observations.title: Chose canonical graph model with methodology projections
observations.content: What: Defined the core architecture for the PWeb business-idea coach as a single canonical graph (problem, segment, value_proposition, solution, channels, revenue, costs, competition, metrics, risks) with each methodology (Lean Canvas, BMC, tree, card) as a pure projection over it. Why: The user wants a natural conversational UX where the AI structures the methodology invisibly, and wants interpolation between multiple methodologies. Where: docs/especificacion-funcional.md sections 3-4. Learned: Projections-as-functions make adding a methodology a mapping, not a migration, and give every view the same version history for free. Hard rule adopted: AI proposes nodes as `inferred`, never writes directly to the source of truth.

observations.title: Decided node edit permissions: direct edit only on confirmed nodes
observations.content: What: Users can directly edit graph nodes only when source is `confirmed`; `inferred` nodes are corrected through conversation. Merge hierarchy is edited > confirmed > inferred. Why: Balances user ownership of the tree against the risk of AI re-extraction overwriting human corrections. Where: docs/especificacion-funcional.md D2, D3, RF-32, RF-33. Learned: The `source` flag on each node also enables provenance traceability (node -> originating message) and gap detection, so one field serves trust, history and coaching.

observations.title: Demo mode became high priority after live evaluation confirmed
observations.content: What: Added Module H (RF-70..RF-74) to the spec: seeded demo account, scripted 90-second walkthrough, no-AI fallback with simulated streaming, reset button, and pre-warm. Why: The university evaluation is a live demo, so an AI provider outage or exhausted free quota is a delivery risk, not a minor bug. Where: docs/especificacion-funcional.md Module H, RNF-15..17, decision L6. Learned: Build the demo path backwards - data model and seeded views first, AI last - so a late AI integration cannot leave the project undemonstrable.

observations.title: Switched BID package manager from npm to pnpm
observations.content: What: Replaced package-lock.json with pnpm-lock.yaml, added packageManager pnpm@11.21.0 to package.json, and documented pnpm in the README. Why: User chose pnpm for the university project. Where: package.json, pnpm-lock.yaml, README.md, commit 1986680. Learned: Node 26 no longer ships corepack, so the packageManager field does not auto-install pnpm - the classmate must run npm install -g pnpm once. The handover zip was verified end to end by extracting to a clean temp dir and running pnpm install --frozen-lockfile, typecheck, tests and build successfully.

observations.title: Scaffolded BID foundation with canonical model and pure projections
observations.content: What: Built the project foundation in PWeb: Next.js 16.4.3 + TypeScript + Tailwind 4 scaffold, hexagonal layer structure (app/application/domain/infrastructure), canonical idea model (10 node types, NodeSource inferred/confirmed/edited), and three pure projections (findGaps, completionRatio, buildTree) with 9 passing Vitest tests. Why: The user asked for architecture and design pattern only, not the full project, so a professor can review it. Where: src/domain/idea/, docs/arquitectura.md, docs/especificacion-funcional.md, README.md. Learned: Next 16 scaffold uses generated LayoutProps types that break `tsc --noEmit` on a fresh clone, so the layout was written with explicit React.ReactNode props instead; next/font was also dropped to avoid build-time network dependency. Three conventional commits created locally; push to Dalan3010/BID blocked because the authenticated gh account (astivens) has READ-only permission.

observations.title: Kept Next.js after explicit challenge; Vite + Hono rejected
observations.content: What: The user reaffirmed Next.js after being presented the alternative Vite + React + Hono. Why: Next.js benefits (SSR, SEO, RSC, image optimization) do not apply to this fully authenticated app, and its server/client boundary adds defense complexity, but the user chose to keep Next.js deliberately. Where: docs/especificacion-funcional.md D5 and decision L7. Learned: The Vercel AI SDK core is framework-agnostic, so streaming is not a Next.js-exclusive argument - that earlier justification was weakened and corrected. Accepted consequence: avoid deep Server Component and implicit caching usage, and be ready to justify the choice in the oral defense. This entry was restored after being overwritten by the pnpm decision, which shared the topic key architecture/stack.

relations.evidence: The new observation is the implementation of the earlier canonical-model decision: it records the actual scaffold and projections built from it.
